chapters.title: Chapter 3680: Point of No Return VIII
paragraphs: [Existence is but a stage. All the living and the dead are merely players on this stage. Every single one will have their entrance—and their exit...]
Those words echoed in the Peacemaker's mind as he sighed, eyes drifting down to the Enneagram pulsing on his chest.

"This was supposed to bring me peace? I don't like it. Where are the last remnants that'll complete you? A full Absolute Complex True Source...that's the only thing that'll give me peace when facing someone like him. And he's leaving, probably to return with reinforcements. We need to get you ready. Fast."
He spoke to the Enneagram as it began to hum, glowing with brilliance that poured across his form before his illusory image vanished, swallowed by the folds of the Nullvein Gravewake.
Within the weavings of the Wheel's flow.
In the Prime Frequency of the End.
The Infiniverse Megalos.
The Infiniverse Megalos could shrink to the size of a grain of sand, yet span across uncharted light-years.
There, in a far-flung corner, the Queen of Matter hovered, studying the massive Vein in the shape of an infinity symbol.
Books spun excitedly around her- each one alive with pulsing light- as she floated in a white dress that shimmered like the remnants of forgotten stars.
"Where to start? Where to start! The lost Harem members? The only Son of the True Emperor of Quintessence? The left-behind Primogenitors? The hot beach boy, Erikson? Ayame? Ugh, I can't choose!"
She smiled, twirling. So many fables she'd only read about and now, she could finally meet them.
But then, her laughter faded into a sigh.
"I know the fate of existence is kind of... hanging by a thread. Is now really the time to meet my heroes?"
What she wanted to do and what she should do clashed inside her.
And yet... her resolve hardened.
"The True Emperor of Quintessence will handle Bob and any other existential messes. I'll help in my own way. I don't need to change who I am, do I? Especially since I have this..."
She turned, glancing over her shoulder.
Behind her dress stretched illusory strings-vast, radiant threads connecting her to the very Infiniverse Megalos. Her Source had been altered permanently by its power.
Her Complexity and Purity surged upward. She was rising into the realm of those she'd once called legends...eventually anyways.
And if that was the case-
"I'll meet all those I only read about before. And I'll start with..."
She opened a glowing book. Her hand pressed a name that lit up in starlit gold.
Shadow Guard, Night.
"Huhu... huhu! She must have written volumes on Queen Adelaide and the others! You're first."
She shot forward like a comet, her Source guiding her straight to the Fable she longed to meet.
A short distance away, still within the Megalos...
An illusory figure- the Infiniverse Megalos Body, watched it all with calm poise. Her expression thoughtful, her eyes shifted to a distant corner of reality before she spoke aloud.
"Master, I wish to come with you. To see what you are about to see."
Her voice sent a message across Existence.
To Noah.
What he was about to witness?
It was located within the True Frequency of the Singed.
The Absolute Complex True Source.
The Wheel of Existence.
She didn't have to wait long.
Noah replied simply.
"Come, then."
Existence buzzed.
Complexity pulsed.
And then, she disappeared.
In the True Frequency of the Singed.
Noah flew forward, streaking across seas of flames- waves growing more intense and more concentrated with every mile.
White-gold gave way to pure white. The color of the Heart of Existence itself.
The further he went, the more condensed and pure the flames became.
Until...
A rift appeared in the distance.
Nothing grand—just a simple white tear in space, exuding terrifying purity.
Just as he neared, space warped.
And the Infiniverse Megalos Body appeared beside him.
The Infiniverse Megalos Body was akin to an embodiment of boundless reality as she stood like an existential empress woven from the threads of existence itself.

She wore a flowing dress of radiant white and gold, its fabric seemingly spun from the starlight of collapsed Megalos. Inlaid across the dress were countless gems shaped like endless loops- symbols of infinity that shimmered with shifting hues, each gem echoing a different Pantheonic Megalos within the Infiniverse.
Her hair, a cascading waterfall of white brilliance, fell past her shoulders like the remnants of forgotten mana. Her gaze was ageless as her eyes exuded wisdom, command, and unshakable poise.
She had come entirely ready to see the core of the Absolute Complex True Source!
Noah smiled, extending his hand.
She took it, serene and steady.
Together, they walked forward.
Past waves of roaring complexity.
And into the white rift that only revealed itself in the deepest core of the True Frequency of the Singed.
Together... they stepped through.
HUUM!
Their very weavings trembled and vibrated as purity and complexity slammed against them like tidal waves.
Had they come without the protection of a True Source, they would have perished instantly.
As the barrage settled, Noah opened his eyes.
Before him lay an endless sea of white and gold, glowing with impossible brilliance and larger than many Frequencies of Existence combined.
And within this sea...floated fragments.
Remnants of a shattered Wheel.
White spokes. Gold spokes. Silver spokes. Scattered traces and ancient pieces- drifting, suspended, across the existential tide.
Yet in the far distance...
He saw it.
A smidge of something enormous.
Something whole.
Not shattered.
Not fractured.
A corner- just a glimpse- of an intact white-gold Wheel. A genuine Wheel of Existence.
But even that was not what held his gaze.
At the very center of the white-gold sea...between them and the Wheel...
Stood a man.
An old man, with wisps of white hair.
He wore a simple robe of white. A golden blindfold veiled his face- his wrinkled skin glowing faintly with serenity and age.
A blindfolded elder, standing where the core of the Wheel of Existence should be.
Noah's eyes narrowed.
Because the Purity radiating from this being...
It surpassed anyone he had ever encountered so far!

chapters.title: Chapter 3681: The Breaking of The Wheel I
paragraphs: An old man with white hair and a white robe, with a golden blindfold on his face.
Noah looked at such a being as they floated serenely in a sea of white-gold brilliance.
Everything around seemed filled with waves of radiant purity, and this being himself seemed to account for more than half of all that purity.
It was an existence that stood in an area which contained the core weavings of the very Wheel of Existence.
So what exactly could such a being represent?
Noah was not a fan of riddles as he and the Infiniverse Megalos Body moved closer across the vast white-gold sea while Noah's voice echoed out.
"An old man with a blindfold where the very core of the weavings of the Wheel is... who might Sir be?"
His tone was that of calm, regal dignity blooming as he asked such a question.
And opposite them, the old man did not raise his gaze or look toward them, as if he were truly blind.
He simply remained in his current position, floating while standing within an endless sea of purity.
His lips moved as he replied with an ancient voice, and if one heard it, they could distinctly notice the fact that such a voice... had not been used frequently.
As if the speaker had not opened his mouth for millions—or billions—of years.
It carried that sense of age and profundity!
"I am The Witness."
The Witness!
A grandiose distinction for any entity that would be in a place deeper than even the Origin Singed had been.
Noah was focused on this being, as his own distinction as the Weaver of Existence sought to unravel and understand the identity... of everything before him.

Meanwhile, the figure of the Infiniverse Megalos Body wasn't even looking at the old man, as her gaze was on the distant, massive section of the white-gold Wheel of Existence swimming in this vast and endless sea of purity.
This was her main focus, as she was here to see and understand what it meant to be an Absolute Complex True Source of Existence!
"The Witness..."
Noah said these words with care as he proceeded to continue.

"And what exactly does The Witness... witness? I deal with a great deal of mysteries and complexities every single day—lately, I find myself liking simplicity and answers to mysteries more than anything."
His words echoed out as he affirmed that the being he was looking at... had a level of purity that exceeded the Quasi-Resplendent Monad that was the Great Beyonder at this moment.
If their power was so high, were they the actual final defender of the Wheel of Existence?
If Bob had managed to get through, would this be the final safeguard the Wheel of Existence had to stop everything?
After the old man was asked such a question, his lips formed a wizened, crescent smile as he waved his hands.

"I see histories old and young. I see weavings of existence that occur, and countless others that do not occur. I witness the flow of the Wheel of Existence, as well as the entities swimming within this flow, making up an interconnected web of existence. I witness the feats of men and women across countless Frequencies of the Wheel. I witness the feats of... Noah Osmont and all the possibilities he could be. I witness the feats of the Infiniverse Megalos and all that she could be. Would you like to see all the possibilities that I witness?"
HUUUM!
Grandiose words that caused Noah's mind to buzz echoed out from this being as he asked whether Noah would like to see the countless possibilities he witnessed.
And at such a question, Noah became stern as he replied calmly:
"Humor me."
The old man who could not see, The Witness, nodded as he waved his hands, causing the eruption of countless illusory screens to fill everything around him.
The illusory screens showed a great deal of things, but at this moment, the face of the Infiniverse Megalos Body filled the screens!
One screen showed her in the Expanses, as she alone stood against Watchers of the Wheelomachy while devouring everything around her.
One screen showed her in the Megalos Beyond, standing before a massive Pantheon that swallowed everything—countless Outerversal Morphons standing against her.
Another screen showed the Infiniverse Megalos Body radiating a terrifying level of power, her mouth wide open, akin to an existential vacuum, as she swallowed an entire Frequency of Existence.

In many of the illusory screens displaying variations of the Infiniverse Megalos, she was conducting different versions of actions—but for the most part... the vast majority showed her devouring the very weavings of existence themselves into her being.
"I witness the Echoes of Existence of the one you brought here."
The Witness spoke as he waved his hand and the illusory screens changed.
"I witness the Echoes of Existence of the one you walk with across Frequencies, right now devouring Shattered Remnants of the Wheel."
The many illusory screens shifted to now display... Ruination.
Now they displayed her figure in multiple forms. In one screen, she was waving her hands toward an entire Frequency of Existence as it was painted red and began to descend into ruin.
In another illusory screen, she sat upon a crimson throne inside Megalos Nihilos, as legions of creatures born of anti-matter swirled around her.
In many other screens, she was shown within the lands of Hell Terra Firma, her figure crossing through while followed by countless races of beings.
In one screen, she was a Primordial Cosmic Treasure that remained floating inside the universe—imposing cycles of ruin again and again... and again.
It showed countless possibilities and variations, as Noah looked at all of them with a cold gaze and spoke out.
"Echoes of Existence?"
The Witness had called them Echoes of Existence.
And he nodded at Noah's question as he replied.

"Yes. Echoes. Possibilities of what was, or what could be. For some, they are parallel versions of the existence they are. You might even possibly see or observe them within the Veiled Frequencies of Existence. In the Unstable Frequencies of Possibilities. Would you like to see your own possibilities? Your own Echoes of Existence?"
The Witness asked such a question as Noah's gaze became unfathomably stern, and yet... he still nodded!

chapters.title: Chapter 3682: The Breaking of the Wheel II
paragraphs: The old man with the blindfold waved his hands again, as the screens proceeded to change one more time.
Countless screens—by the thousands—flickered and changed from displaying variations of Ruination. And yet when they changed to display Noah's variations...
The countless screens were actually blank.
They showed nothing.
There was only a single screen reflecting the same image of him at this very moment!
All of the other screens had absolutely nothing.
The scene was heart-shaking.
The Witness held an impassive gaze as he revealed a singular screen of variation—a singular screen of possibility.

"Out there, across the endless threads of reality, there are countless possibilities and parallel weavings of existence. And yet for you... your possibilities seem to be dragged in and contained within a single weaving of existence. Why is that?"
The Witness asked that question.

Out there, across the parallel weavings of existence—across the Frequencies of Existence—one might find different versions of Barbatos, Adelaide, Athena... even Echoes of Existence for the Infiniverse Megalos and Ruination.
Reflections of what they could be, based on their current weavings of complexity.
But they wouldn't be able to find Noah.
And as the question settled like thunder in the silence, Noah's eyes flashed with sharp brilliance, his words slicing through the moment like a tyrannical blade.

"Should the Witness not be the one to tell me why and explain these mysteries? You stand at the very core of the Wheel of Existence. The things you see and know should be innumerable, right? So tell me—what theories do you have? What possibilities can I ponder myself?"
He asked with a cold gaze and the old man in the blindfold simply... shook his head.
"I do not know."
HUUM!
"The Wheel of Existence does not know."
WAA!

"You rose and entered the flow of the Wheel in a way that forced even the Wheel to look at you, recognize you...to accept you. I believe you were always there. You were born of its weavings...and yet somehow, your possibilities and variations were nowhere to be found. I do not know. And neither does the Wheel. There was a time I worked very, very hard to Witness where those possibilities might have been as you began to encompass a dense flow of Existence..."
As he spoke, the old man with the golden blindfold waved his hand—and three of the once-empty screens filled with life.
They showed...Noah on his Blue Planet.
One screen showed him living peacefully with his mother and father. A harmonious, happy family. It showed him growing up... becoming a doctor.
No apocalypse.
No Beasts or Demons.
Another screen showed him burying his parents while still very young. The weight of loss forging him into a tyrant—an underground boss who lived for control.
A third screen revealed him with a family of his own. A woman with golden hair. A pet eagle. Three children gathered around a dining table—laughing, eating, living.
The Witness displayed these as he slowly shook his head.
"The amount of weavings required just to pull up these three... could birth a thousand Frequencies."

"And these possibilities... they only existed before you ever touched Mana. After that, not even the Wheel could find a single Echo of your Existence. Even those of immense power leave variants—trails of Echoes. Look around you. They all do. But you... don't. Are you..."
Now the old man hesitated, as if unsure how to ask the question that weighed down his chest.
Noah remained still.
And after a pause that echoed across Existence, the question finally fell.
"Are you... alive?"
BOOM!
The Witness, who stood at the core of the Wheel of Existence, was asking Noah... if he was alive.
BZZZT!

The figure of the Infiniverse Megalos Body turned cold at the question. A terrifying complexity radiated from her, pressing down on The Witness like a storm. Her energy whispered one simple thing- How dare you?!
And still, The Witness bore it, shaking his head slowly.

"Don't misunderstand me. It's a genuine question. Look at the Living... and the Dead. The Dead have fewer possibilities—just faint Echoes. But before they were dead, they brimmed with potential. Because all Dead Things... were once alive. All broken Wheels of Existence... were once whole. Do you know why they died? Do you know the true nature of the Wheels of Existence?"
The true nature of the Wheels of Existence.
Noah's mind buzzed with the weight of it, his thoughts vibrating as he answered coldly.
"Then enlighten me."
The old man smiled.

His golden blindfold flickered as he waved his hand once more- causing the countless screens to vanish, replacing them with what had always surrounded them- the endless white-gold sea and the shattered Remnants of the Wheel.
The Spokes. The Traces. The Pieces.
And far away... the distant white-gold Wheel, only a single section of it visible.
The Witness extended a hand to all of it, speaking with a voice carved from utter majesty.
"For there to be remnants... something must have broken. For there to be shattered pieces of the Wheel of Existence... the Wheel itself must have fractured."
WAA!
The Wheel of Existence had to be shattered... for Traces and Pieces to drift across Frequencies.
Noah's weavings pulsed.
His very distinction as the Weaver of Existence whispered that these words... were truth.
And yet...
He turned his head to stare at the distant white-gold Wheel, still so pristine. Still so whole. And the blindfold on The Witness shimmered as he spoke again—serene and powerful.
"Shall I show you... the first breaking of the Wheel?"
HUUM!
As those words rang out, a colossal screen of brilliance bloomed behind him—stretching the length of an entire Omniverse.
Lesser minds would have shattered just trying to comprehend it.
But for Noah... and the Infiniverse Megalos...
It was but a glance.
A glance that held everything.
And on that screen—spanning stars and systems and the spaces between...
He saw...
A radiant, verdant Wheel of Existence.
Unfathomably vast.
Floating serenely in an endless emerald sea.
Its colossal spokes blazed with quintillions of ancient runes, and towering waves of complexity rippled around it—each surge humming with dense concentrations of impossibly pure existence.
It pulsed.
With life.
With serenity.
With transcendence.
With power that defied all reason.
A Green Wheel of Existence.
And The Witness simply said...
"This... was the first breaking of the Wheel."

Reflections of what they could be, based on their current weavings of complexity.
But they wouldn't be able to find Noah.
And as the question settled like thunder in the silence, Noah's eyes flashed with sharp brilliance, his words slicing through the moment like a tyrannical blade.
"Should the Witness not be the one to tell me why and explain these mysteries?
You stand at the very core of the Wheel of Existence.
The things you see and know should be innumerable, right?
So tell me—what theories do you have?
What possibilities can I ponder myself?"
He asked with a cold gaze and the old man in the blindfold simply... shook his head.
"I do not know."
HUUM!
"The Wheel of Existence does not know."
WAA!
"You rose and entered the flow of the Wheel in a way that forced even the Wheel to look at you, recognize you...to accept you.
I believe you were always there.
You were born of its weavings...and yet somehow, your possibilities and variations were nowhere to be found.
I do not know.
And neither does the Wheel.
There was a time I worked very, very hard to Witness where those possibilities might have been as you began to encompass a dense flow of Existence..."
As he spoke, the old man with the golden blindfold waved his hand—and three of the once-empty screens filled with life.
They showed...Noah on his Blue Planet.
One screen showed him living peacefully with his mother and father.
A harmonious, happy family.
It showed him growing up... becoming a doctor.
No apocalypse.
No Beasts or Demons.
Another screen showed him burying his parents while still very young.
The weight of loss forging him into a tyrant—an underground boss who lived for control.
A third screen revealed him with a family of his own.
A woman with golden hair.
A pet eagle.
Three children gathered around a dining table—laughing, eating, living.
The Witness displayed these as he slowly shook his head.
"The amount of weavings required just to pull up these three... could birth a thousand Frequencies."
"And these possibilities... they only existed before you ever touched Mana.
After that, not even the Wheel could find a single Echo of your Existence.
Even those of immense power leave variants—trails of Echoes.
Look around you.
They all do.
But you... don't.
Are you..."
Now the old man hesitated, as if unsure how to ask the question that weighed down his chest.
Noah remained still.
And after a pause that echoed across Existence, the question finally fell.
"Are you... alive?"
BOOM!
The Witness, who stood at the core of the Wheel of Existence, was asking Noah... if he was alive.
BZZZT!
The figure of the Infiniverse Megalos Body turned cold at the question.
A terrifying complexity radiated from her, pressing down on The Witness like a storm.
Her energy whispered one simple thing- How dare you?!
And still, The Witness bore it, shaking his head slowly.
"Don't misunderstand me.
It's a genuine question.
Look at the Living... and the Dead.
The Dead have fewer possibilities—just faint Echoes.
But before they were dead, they brimmed with potential.
Because all Dead Things... were once alive.
All broken Wheels of Existence... were once whole.
Do you know why they died?
Do you know the true nature of the Wheels of Existence?"
The true nature of the Wheels of Existence.
Noah's mind buzzed with the weight of it, his thoughts vibrating as he answered coldly.
"Then enlighten me."
The old man smiled.

His golden blindfold flickered as he waved his hand once more- causing the countless screens to vanish, replacing them with what had always surrounded them- the endless white-gold sea and the shattered Remnants of the Wheel.
The Spokes.
The Traces.
The Pieces.
And far away... the distant white-gold Wheel, only a single section of it visible.
The Witness extended a hand to all of it, speaking with a voice carved from utter majesty.
"For there to be remnants... something must have broken.
For there to be shattered pieces of the Wheel of Existence... the Wheel itself must have fractured."
WAA!
The Wheel of Existence had to be shattered... for Traces and Pieces to drift across Frequencies.
Noah's weavings pulsed.
His very distinction as the Weaver of Existence whispered that these words... were truth.
And yet...
He turned his head to stare at the distant white-gold Wheel, still so pristine.
Still so whole.
And the blindfold on The Witness shimmered as he spoke again—serene and powerful.
"Shall I show you... the first breaking of the Wheel?"
HUUM!
As those words rang out, a colossal screen of brilliance bloomed behind him—stretching the length of an entire Omniverse.
Lesser minds would have shattered just trying to comprehend it.
But for Noah... and the Infiniverse Megalos...
It was but a glance.
A glance that held everything.
And on that screen—spanning stars and systems and the spaces between...
He saw...
A radiant, verdant Wheel of Existence.
Unfathomably vast.
Floating serenely in an endless emerald sea.
Its colossal spokes blazed with quintillions of ancient runes, and towering waves of complexity rippled around it—each surge humming with dense concentrations of impossibly pure existence.
It pulsed.
With life.
With serenity.
With transcendence.
With power that defied all reason.
A Green Wheel of Existence.
And The Witness simply said...
"This... was the first breaking of the Wheel."

chapters.title: Chapter 3683: The Breaking of the Wheel III
paragraphs: The First Breaking of the Wheel!
The Witness uttered those words just as, behind him, a massive screen the size of an Omniverse bloomed into existence.
But it didn't feel like any random screen.
It felt real.
It felt like they were looking at a grand record etched into the very fabric of existence.

And as if to confirm it, Noah and the Infiniverse Megalos Body locked eyes with the golden-blindfolded figure of the Witness. In his ancient voice, he called out to them, green-gold tendrils emanating from his hands, floating mere inches away.
"If you allow me... you can experience the Record of the First Breaking of the Wheel yourself."
"As the Witness, I have seen it. I have preserved it. And at this moment, I can show it in a true sense by allowing you to experience it yourselves."
To experience the First Breaking of the Wheel.
Even the idea was terrifying. Noah's weavings of existence burned brilliantly, his True Sources analyzing the green-gold tendril before him as he coldly reached for it.
That tendril radiated a terrifying purity and complexity far beyond the Mythic Signature of the Great Beyonder.
It held a True Source Noah hadn't yet fully understood, but he recognized it with a sense of familiarity.
He gave a light nod to his Construct beside him. As he grabbed the tendril, an incandescent green-gold brilliance bathed everything nearby.
And then, part of his consciousness was pulled elsewhere.
To another weaving of existence entirely.
To the flow of an age lost to eons.
To the record of the First Breaking of the Wheel!
"Haha, Little Witness, are you really dozing off right now? Shouldn't you act out your name and title and be here to witness this grandiose event?"
The voice stirred Noah from what felt like a deep reverie, an impossibly long dream.
HUUUM!
In the depths of his existence, the stellar obsidian radiance of his True Source of Existence buzzed, anchoring him. He knew who he was. This was a record. This was the dream.
He spread his senses outward.
He was in a small body- young, maybe a teenager. But his eyes couldn't see.
A green blindfold wrapped around them, tied neatly at the back of his head. His robe was simple—white and green—covering him from top to bottom.
Even when he looked inward, he found a calm, silent True Source at the Nascent Source-Bearer Complexity level.
It was... the True Source of Continuity.
This was the True Source of the Witness!
But the real shock was his surroundings.
An endless green sea.
Scattered across it like radiant archipelagos were Frequency Havens—self-contained micro-frequencies tethered to the sea's flow, all converging toward a resplendent, green Wheel of Existence.

The Frequency Havens pulsed with their own unique Source structures. One was a floating citadel of harmonic crystal and firelight. Another, a storm reef of volatile plasma and temporal sand. Some shimmered with lunar ice that sang waves of complexity. Others swirled through labyrinths of compressed gravity and spectral flora of existence.
And they were guarded not by ordinary entities, but by those who burned with the light of True Sources.
The most powerful of them were Resplendent Monads and Converged Architects.
Monads and Architects.
Though Noah's eyes were blind, his senses- his True Source- saw clearly. He could feel the presence and expressions of dozens of these entities.
An overwhelming intensity of Purity. A staggering depth of Complexity.

Some sat calmly atop their Frequency Havens. Others talked among themselves or with those of lower standing. On many havens, Noah sensed Resplendent Monads smiling and conversing with Harmonized Sourcebound Icons and Nascent Source-Bearers, who gazed at them with respect.
This was a different age.
A different record, a different weaving of existence- one where beings of Average, Moderate, and High Purity and Complexity existed in breathtaking abundance.
Even the Frequency Haven he stood upon spanned the size of a standard Omniverse- its complexity exponentially greater.
Waves of verdant-gold light shimmered around him. Complexity...was everywhere.
Even the one who woke him...
Noah turned to find a burly, muscular man in a loose, stellar green robe. His body burned with green flames, vibrant with life and vitality.
When he clapped Noah on the back- lightly, the tremors threatened to fracture his source if it had been any harder.
Profundity radiated from him. His eyes, expectant and vibrant, glowed with High Purity and Complexity. He was both a Resplendent Monad and a Converged Architect.

"All who wanted to be here to witness the Wheel's change are here," he said. "Many came from the Infinite Ravines- trading places to witness this moment themselves. What do you think, Little Witness? What are we about to witness with the Wheel of Existence?"
The terrifying existence posed the question, and Noah found his lips moving as though this young body were playing out a perfect record.

"How should I know? We're all just watching the First of Existence. And Monad Romulus... I know you know exactly what level of purity and complexity your source has reached. If you keep hitting me like that, you'll shatter my weavings next time."
His voice was laced with annoyance and grumbling- completely unlike the deep, ancient tone of the Witness he and the Infiniverse Megalos Body had observed not long ago.
And still, despite the grumblings, Monad Romulus only laughed and beckoned to others gathered in the distance.

"Hey, Monad Gideon, Architect Reyna! Come give this kid a few more smacks. He doesn't seem to know what's good for him. I was helping his True Source grow stronger with every slap- and he complains about it!"
Laughter rippled through the Resplendent Monads and Converged Architects as the Witness turned toward them with a mixture of fondness and frustration.
They were his mentors. His teachers. The ones who had guided him across existence.
He knew they meant well. And now?
Now, he had to take this moment seriously.
He had to Witness.
Time passed as those terrifyingly complex entities communicated, a display of harmony and wonder in this forgotten age... until finally...
"Oh... it begins!"

chapters.title: Chapter 3684: The Breaking of the Wheel IV
paragraphs: The voice of Resplendent Monad Romulus rang out from this Frequency Haven, echoing across the vibrant, stellar-green sea.
His gaze and the gaze of many others turned toward the distant, verdant Wheel of Existence that had begun to radiate a terrifying brilliance.
The transformation of the Wheel of Existence.
With their level of power, they all felt the shift coming, but none of them knew what it truly meant, or what would come next.

They only knew that the Wheel of Existence, the very force that had shouldered and sheltered them since their youth like an umbrella woven from stars as they grew in power and complexity- had to transform.
It wasn't even a matter of choice. This change... whatever it was... had to happen.
It was bound to happen.
And they were here to witness it. To support it.
Would it hold the answer to the Infinite Ravines and the unending assaults of the Living and the Dead?
None of them knew.
So, they watched.
And then...
HUUUM!
Everything began to tremble. The Wheel of Existence became suffused with a terrifying magnitude of complexity.
The Wheel seemed to gather all that it was- all that it had been- as it surged with a brilliance far greater than anything it had shown before.
Beside him, Resplendent Monad Romulus chuckled softly, casting his gaze toward a distant point where a lone entity floated unaccompanied, untouchable.
"Even that guy couldn't stay away, huh?"
He spoke casually, but his words held weight. Noah turned to look, his eyes pulsing because even though this figure didn't radiate outward light or display overwhelming power...
When one's gaze truly landed on him, the purity and complexity that being held... exceeded that of any living Resplendent Monad or Converged Architect.
A man in a stellar-green robe. His face was mostly obscured, yet from this far distance, Noah could see his eyes.
Eyes holding a deep, ancient sadness.
As if... he already knew what was coming.
His deeply green eyes pulsed with an intensity Noah couldn't withstand for long.
The transformation had begun.
The Wheel was changing.
A storm of complexity bloomed and converged from every direction as the booming sound of the Wheel turning echoed out.
The Wheel of Existence... was turning.
And even the Resplendent Monads and Converged Architects fell silent.

All watched as the verdant Wheel completed a full turn. The spokes, the surface, every intricate rune etched onto it glowed—each one alive with a level of complexity unattainable by any entity. A complexity that only an Absolute Complex True Source could reach.
And then, the Wheel- overflowing with unimaginable complexity- could no longer hold it in.
In a brief, breathless moment...
It flashed.

A wave of blinding brilliance burst outward, revealing quintillions upon quintillions of green threads extending from the Wheel- threads that touched every True Source in this place, and countless more across frequencies and realities.
As if it was borrowing the blessing and complexity of all those it once shielded... and those still seeking shelter beneath it.

Noah watched as a pillar of verdant light erupted around the Wheel. Its surface began to change. Thick green lines formed—intricate and deliberate—as if the Wheel was forging something grander than itself.
Every observer felt it. Their complexities buzzed. Their souls stirred. The gains they could draw from this moment... they would ponder for eons.
Then, in the next moment...
BZZT!
The brilliant green pillar of light distorted and fizzled.
Something was...missing.
The complexity wasn't enough.
Something hadn't been achieved.
And then...
Everything turned.
It happened far too fast for anyone to stop it.
The pillar fizzled out—and a massive fissure split the Wheel of Existence from top to bottom.
CRACK!
As if his soul had been split, Noah whispered in the body of the Witness.
"AAH!"
"NO!" Beside him, Romulus and the others roared in horror. Their bodies ignited with power as they surged toward the Wheel.
But it was too late.
The crack became an unraveling.
And in the next instant, the verdant Wheel of Existence shattered—splintering into countless fragments!
It was...the breaking.
The Breaking of the Wheel.
Noah saw it all.
The Witness stood frozen, anchored atop the Frequency Haven, watching as the impossible unfolded.
No one had expected this.
They had all anticipated a transformation. A rebirth. Something greater.
But never this.
The full breaking of the Wheel was too immense.
It unleashed a blinding brilliance—raw complexity surging outward with a light that blinded even the Witness.
He felt it.
The existence around him vanished. He couldn't see. Couldn't feel.
Even the blindfold over his eyes—he couldn't sense it.
Seconds. Minutes. Days. Eons.
Time lost all meaning.
And then...
Sensation returned.
The Witness inhaled—foreign air filling his lungs. His chest burned, his True Source strained under the weight of new, unfamiliar changes.
Familiar, yet not.
And when his senses returned fully...
His body trembled.
He looked around.
Nothing.
No one.
He was alone.
Even the green sea...
No- it was no longer green.
Before his very eyes, the sea shifted from verdant purity to a crimson hue of brilliance.
He turned, and where the great Wheel had once stood majestic and glorious...
A new crimson Wheel bloomed.
A newborn Wheel, glowing faintly.
Its complexity was far less than the one before. A fraction of the verdant titan that came before it.
But none of that mattered.
The Witness wept.
Tears streamed down his face as his senses reached across the sea, over shattered pieces of the Wheel, broken remnants of Frequency Havens, and wild pulses of incomplete True Sources.
"Monad Romulus?! Monad Gideon?!"
The Witness cried out with all the complexity of his True Source of Continuity.
But there was no answer.
He had seen the Breaking of the Wheel—and now... every person he'd ever known was gone.
He could still sense the echoes of their lives.
He, who had never seen since the day he was born, felt the truth. He instinctively knew.
They weren't dead.
Their True Sources hadn't collapsed.
So where were they?
And why was he the only one left?
"Monad Romulus...!"
A deep, broken cry tore from his soul—but no answer came.
Only a blooming, crimson Wheel of Existence remained.
The prior form...
Had undergone the Breaking.

chapters.title: Chapter 3685: The Breaking of the Wheel V
paragraphs: Green turned to crimson.
Vast stretches of sea adopted that crimson allure of brilliance as the hum of a silent, glowing Wheel stretched out across existence.
Everything looked altered- and yet, somehow, not. Inside the Witness, Noah felt it all.

He felt the Breaking of the Wheel with his very existence as his mind surged with static and wonder, the scene replaying over his existence again and again as it was both horrific and beautiful at the same time.
A failed transformation.
But a transformation into what?
And if it failed, how many times had this happened before? Because in this moment, there wasn't just a crimson Wheel of Existence... but a white-gold one.
So just how many Breakings had there been?
How many failures?
And where had all the powerful Resplendent Monads and Converged Architects gone? Where had those beneath them in power gone?
The Breaking didn't destroy them. But it was as if the strongest beings tied to the Wheel were displaced—flung to unknown realms every time a Breaking occurred.
As these questions churned, Noah felt the same desolation and quiet grief the Witness carried.
The green blindfold, shaped by the surrounding sources, slowly changed—its verdant hue bleeding into the crimson shade of the sea around them.
The Witness was completely blind, relying only on his source. His head turned in the direction of the slowly spinning crimson Wheel as he wondered.
As he grieved.
As he cried.
And from then on, he continued to Witness.
HUUUM!
Other weavings of existence thrummed in the moments that followed as the surrounding weavings fractured and broke.
The record of an age—one far older than comprehension—came to an end.
It showed glimpses of beings who had existed before the First Breaking of the Wheel.
Beings far more powerful than anything currently within the flow of the Wheel of Existence.
And because he had Witnessed this... Noah's weavings of existence began to spark with grand possibilities.
As the ancient record shattered, his essence snapped back into the present—and even as it did, he could still feel the changes and wonder from what he'd just experienced.
|The True Source of Continuity has been understood under a different definition from the True Source of the Witness.|
He had lived the First Breaking of the Wheel by merging with the body of the Witness.

And the burning True Source of this being was open to him—his to explore—because for that brief span of time, it felt like his own body. He'd understood the very definition of Continuity from someone else's eyes.
Noah's continuity stemmed from the very pillars that held up the foundation of the Infiniverse Megalos.
Pillars like Entropy, Relativity, Manadynamics, and more.
And now, his Pathway toward the True Source of Continuity absorbed a new definition, reshaping itself.
But that wasn't all.
|You Witnessed the weavings of the Resplendent Monad Romulus and gazed upon his True Source of Entropy.|
|A possible definition of Entropy tracing back to the First Breaking of the Wheel has been obtained by your weavings of existence.|
HUUM!
His essence thrummed with new potential. His gains weren't singular.
But still contained.
Because in the next moment, his weavings awoke once more—this time in the radiant, white-gold seas of brilliance.

Beside him, the Infiniverse Megalos Body released a slight tremble. Her eyes shimmered with returning light—her weavings reigniting with terrifying brilliance. Noah had no clue what truths she'd faced in the vision of the First Breaking.
But then... his mind buzzed again as she began to share her knowledge and memory of it.
Noah had taken over the Witness to observe—but where had she been?
That question lingered until the unthinkable happened.
The Witness had layered the weavings of the Infiniverse Megalos Body... onto the First Wheel of Existence.
The Verdant Wheel.
Unlike Noah—who only observed—she had lived the First Breaking.
Her weavings trembled. Noah's expression turned grim as his gaze shifted to the distant Witness. Even with his golden blindfold, the ravines of sadness surrounding him were palpable.

His power was immense. He had chosen Noah to descend into his younger body to observe that cataclysmic moment. And somehow, he had also allowed the Infiniverse Megalos Body's weavings to be projected onto the Wheel that broke.
And whatever repercussions or catastrophes might result from this were completely unknown. Because in that moment... the Infiniverse Megalos Body stood frozen.
As if observing and feeling the Breaking had done something unexplainable to her!
Amid it all, the Witness spoke again.

"That was the first Breaking of the Wheel. Back then, none of us knew what the change would bring...or what the transformation would birth. All those who were there to witness it vanished—except me. Where they went, I can only theorize. But after watching a brand-new Wheel spin and turn, I believed the failure to evolve... released a surge of unfathomable complexity that wiped the slate clean. Yet the Breaking didn't decimate those tied to the former Wheel. It didn't kill. It sent them—to other signatures of life."

"I told myself they had been scattered across different weavings. Different Wheels of Existence. I can not say if it is true, but... it comforted me back then. Since that day, I have Witnessed. After the First Breaking, I stayed. I watched the Wheel turn and weave. I witnessed new True Sources bloom under the threads of an Absolute Complex Source."
"And during all that time... my greatest fear remained the Infinite Ravines. But when I visited their many Gateway Domus... I found no Living. No Dead. For years...for countless years."
When the Witness said that, Noah's weavings pulsed violently.
He remembered something crucial mentioned in the record of the First Breaking.

That there were beings left behind in the Ravines... to defend- and they were even capable of easily switching their position with those inside the Wheel of Existence and going back and forth...since there were many of them to defend.
To defend against both the Living and the Dead.
Entities tied to Living True Sources... and those bound to Dead ones had all been attacking the Infinite Ravines!

chapters.title: Chapter 3686: The Breaking of the Wheel VI
paragraphs: After the First Breaking of the Wheel, there was a disappearance of everything within the Infinite Ravines, and nothing appeared again for countless years that followed.
When it seemed like the Witness was about to continue speaking on his own accord, Noah stopped him gently with a question.
"In the previous records I observed," he said softly, "it was mentioned that there was a defense against both the Living and the Dead in the Infinite Ravines. Why is that?"
It was a critical question.
The Witness smiled before responding.

"Even we did not understand it then. We would battle Harmonized Sourcebound Icons... and occasionally Converged Architects and Monads—brimming with life—who had crossed the Nullvein Gravewake Folds. They seemed drawn to our Infinite Ravines. Many of them fought with everything they had, saying they simply sought entry into the weavings of the Wheel. But we allowed neither the Living nor the Dead. For even the Dead could mimic the Living... and corrupt all they touched. Yet the reason both were drawn into the Ravines... was due to the brilliant complexity the First Wheel of Existence emanated."
The Nullvein Gravewake Folds.
Scattered memories of that place—collapsed weavings and folded threads of existence—had already begun budding within Noah, even as he shredded records and purified Dead True Sources in the present.
And the Witness's voice pressed on.

"Before its First Breaking, it drew every entity toward it simply because of the immense Purity it held. Before the Breaking. Before the failed transformation. Afterward... there were no more visitors in the Infinite Ravines. It was as if the light from the Wheel was no longer strong enough to draw in anything from the Folds. Only after millions of years—when the Wheel's complexity and purity began rising again—did Dead Things start appearing. No Living ones. And even the Dead were weaker. This... along with my Witnessing of the Second and Third Breakings of the Wheel... allowed me to form a few undeniable conclusions."
Noah's expression shifted at the mention of the Second and Third Breakings.
It hadn't happened just once. It had happened again—and again.
The Witness continued.

"By the time the Dead began being pulled into the Infinite Ravines, new True Sources had begun to bud and rise. They kept the Dead at bay. And because I knew so little at the time, I even descended into the Infinite Ravines myself to ensure all remained as it should. After the First Breaking... the number of beings who could attain the level of Monad or Converged Architect was pitifully small compared to those who existed before the First Breaking. Then came a time I sensed a change. Others sensed it too. They came to the core weavings of the Wheel to observe—curious, but unaware of what was coming."
The Witness's blindfold seemed to grow heavier, his burden too great to name.

"And I was there... when the Second Breaking of the Wheel occurred. And again—I was the only one left. All others were scattered and sent away. The defenders and Dead Things within the Ravines were also expelled. The crimson Wheel cracked and broke... and in its place, a Violet Wheel of Existence bloomed. It was less pure, less complex than the First Verdant Wheel. This time, it took many more millions of years for its purity to rise again. And again, weaker Dead Things came. Even fewer entities could rise to the level of Monad or Converged Architect. None—not a single one—came close to that being who exceeded even Monads before the First Breaking."
Noah remembered.
The green-haired man—the one Monad Romulus had pointed to. A man whose gaze carried the weight of sadness and inevitability, as if he knew what would happen to the Wheel of Existence.
No entity like him had ever risen again.
The Witness's blindfold buzzed softly as he spoke.

"The Third Breaking. The Fourth. The Fifth. Sixth. Seventh. Eighth... They all occurred, one after the other. And each time... the Wheel of Existence lost more of the purity and complexity it had once held during the era of the First Verdant Wheel. Every transformation it attempted afterward failed. I came to understand something: the transformation had to succeed the first time. If the Wheel undergoes a Breaking... then the chances of transformation succeeding after that are nearly nonexistent. And the more it Breaks... the more impossible it becomes. Until..."
He swept his arms across the golden sea around them.
And Noah's eyes widened as he looked out at the countless shattered pieces of the Wheel floating across the horizon... and the distant, white-gold brilliance of the current Wheel of Existence.

"We never knew what the transformation would've brought. But it had to succeed the first time. Since it didn't... I understood that the Wheel was doomed to repeat Breakings. Again and again. And not long ago, I felt it again. The level of complexity and purity of the Wheel behind us... has once more reached a threshold. One that is calling transformation. It could occur in a million years. A thousand. A year. A month. I don't know."
The words he said next nearly made Noah curse aloud.
"I do not know when it will happen. But I do know this—after all the Breakings I have Witnessed, one truth has become clear. This coming Ninth Transformation of the Wheel... is the final one."
HUUM!

"If this transformation is not passed successfully—and I say again, it is nearly impossible—then the Wheel of Existence will Break for the ninth time. And when that happens... it will no longer be a Living Absolute Complex True Source."
"It will finally—and irrevocably—become a Dead Absolute Complex True Source. No more chances. No more transformations. No more Living."
BOOM!
The words were horrific even to hear—and yet, they were spoken.
Noah's eyes gleamed with a fierce, terrifying light as a question surfaced again in his mind.
The question of the Living and the Dead.
Where did the Dead come from?
They were the same.
They were all the products... of the Breakings of the Wheel of Existence!

chapters.title: Chapter 3687: Infiniverse I
paragraphs: A Wheel of Existence actually undergoes a series of transformations—again and again—across its infinite weavings.
The first transformation was meant to succeed.

But when it failed, the Wheel shattered like a shell far too intricate to remain whole. In shedding that immense complexity, another version of itself bloomed—but it was a dim echo. Less pure. Less vast.
Logically, if the transformation couldn't succeed when the Wheel held its peak brilliance and complexity, how could it possibly succeed in a lesser state? The second time. The third. The eighth.
And now, it stood on the edge of a ninth transformation—its final one!
Failure was almost written into its fate.
The Ninth Breaking of the Wheel was bound to happen, and this time with finality!
Noah's eyes simmered, lit with the terrible glow of existence as he thought through it all.

Before the first breaking, the Wheel radiated such complexity, such purity, that it gave rise to Resplendent Monads and Converged Architects. And when that happened, both the living and the dead from the Nullvein Gravewake Folds came for it.
Now? Only a scattered handful of Dead Things drifted toward this fading, depleted golden Wheel—its luster dulled, its complexity diminished.
Even its protectors now mirrored that decay as they weren't that powerful compared to before!
Everything was connected.
Every action met an equal and opposite reaction.

And Noah now stood before the reality that the Ninth Breaking of the Wheel wasn't spoken of as a "transformation" anymore. No. The transformation had become a myth, a laughable impossibility. What remained was collapse.
The collapse of the Wheel of Existence... and with it, everything it held. Every life. Every source. Doomed to fall under the weavings of a Dead Absolute Complex True Source.
He...would not allow it!
His gaze lifted- sharp, burning, unyielding- toward the Witness.
That ancient figure who had been there from the very beginning. From the First Breaking.
The one who had watched it all.
So Noah asked, voice steady, "Across thousands, millions, and billions of years through every breaking—you've just watched. The Ninth and final one is coming. Did you try to stop any of it?"
Did he try?
Such a question cracked the silence. The being in the golden blindfold trembled, ever so slightly. He took a slow, heavy breath—and answered with aching calm.

"I have tried more than you can imagine. I've experimented with Dead Things, their memories, their echoes, all in search of the origin—trying to learn what went wrong. I ventured to the perilous, collapsed weavings of the Nullvein Gravewake Folds... searching, begging for an answer. Over the eons, I've asked myself endlessly—how could the impossible be overcome? And always, the answer circled back to one truth: something must change. A new variable must rise. Whether from within... or from outside the Wheel."
WAA!
As those words hung in the air, his sightless eyes, seeing so much even though they were blind, locked onto Noah.
And the old man continued.
"In the Third Breaking, I observed hopeful possibilities. Entities with curious complexities. I asked myself—Could they be the variable? But no. They weren't.
The Fourth Breaking came. I waited. I watched. And again—nothing.
The Fifth. The Sixth. The Seventh. No true change. No spark."
His voice softened, distant with memory.

"Not until the Eighth. Then... one appeared. A Holder of a True Source of Asche. He reached the Resplendent Monad level. He wasn't cast away like the others—just like me. But even he, in the end, wasn't enough."
He took a moment, then looked into the present.

"And now? This final weaving. This last desperate chance. I asked again—Is there any hope? Or will the Wheel perish into obscurity... while I become the Witness of its final fall... just another Dead Thing?
I asked. I pondered. I witnessed. Waiting for anything... for anyone..."
His voice faltered. Then grew strong.
"And out of nowhere, they appeared.
A Dead Thing...carrying two Dead Absolute Complex True Sources.
A Living Native... with a budding False Absolute Complex True Source.
And then... two Constructs capable of becoming Wheels themselves."
Behind him, illusory screens lit up—massive and otherworldly—revealing the images of Bob, the Peacemaker, Ruination, and the Infiniverse Megalos Body.
"Variables," the Witness whispered, his voice reverent.

"They came from nowhere. The first two were easier to understand. The other two...were not of this weaving. Not even bound to their own paths. They were... controlled by something else. Something even the Wheel itself could not comprehend. An Anomaly that had no echoes. No probabilities. Just impossibility."
His blind gaze fixed fully on Noah.
But Noah remained calm. Cold. Watching.
Variables. Possibilities.
The Witness had watched across eons— and he looked at Bob or the Peacemaker as possibilities. He stood, wondering if Infiniverse Megalos or Ruination were the answer.
But then...
Noah's gaze sharpened.
"You thought Bob might be the Variable? Just because he carried two Dead Absolute Complex True Sources? You continued to watch all he did because of that?"
Silence fell. The Witness could feel the disdain bleeding from Noah's words.
He looked down at his hands as he spoke again—softly.

"I have witnessed quintillions of deaths across these breakings. You and I see the world differently. We act differently. I don't expect you to agree with my choices... but they are my weavings, just as your actions are yours. I may not approve of them... but I would never hold them against you."
Differences. Viewpoints. Actions. Weavings!
Noah's eyes glinted.
"And what actions of mine do you not approve of?"
WAA!
It was a knife-sharp question—and the Witness paused before answering with that same calm, ancient tone.

"It's not a single action. It's your very existence. Your state of being. You are...incomprehensible. As an Anomaly, you add chaos when we need clarity. You birth paradoxes. And binding yourself to the brightest Variables... only deepens the uncertainty.
When the final breaking nears, I believe what is needed is certainty.
Not Anomalies.
But again... I don't hold it against y—"
"You've talked enough."
HUUM!
A new voice rang out—cutting cleanly through the moment.
It wasn't Noah.
And it wasn't the Witness.
The Infiniverse Megalos Body stepped forward, standing tall beside Noah. Her eyes shimmered—glorious and unfathomable—brimming with the cold, unrelenting brilliance of Megalos.
And they were locked entirely on the Witness.

Entities with curious complexities.
I asked myself—Could they be the variable?
But no.
They weren't.
The Fourth Breaking came.
I waited.
I watched.
And again—nothing.
The Fifth.
The Sixth.
The Seventh.
No true change.
No spark."
His voice softened, distant with memory.
"Not until the Eighth.
Then... one appeared.
A Holder of a True Source of Asche.
He reached the Resplendent Monad level.
He wasn't cast away like the others—just like me.
But even he, in the end, wasn't enough."
He took a moment, then looked into the present.
"And now?
This final weaving.
This last desperate chance.
I asked again—Is there any hope?
Or will the Wheel perish into obscurity... while I become the Witness of its final fall... just another Dead Thing?
I asked.
I pondered.
I witnessed.
Waiting for anything... for anyone..."
His voice faltered.
Then grew strong.
"And out of nowhere, they appeared.
A Dead Thing...carrying two Dead Absolute Complex True Sources.
A Living Native... with a budding False Absolute Complex True Source.
And then... two Constructs capable of becoming Wheels themselves."
Behind him, illusory screens lit up—massive and otherworldly—revealing the images of Bob, the Peacemaker, Ruination, and the Infiniverse Megalos Body.
"Variables," the Witness whispered, his voice reverent.
"They came from nowhere.
The first two were easier to understand.
The other two...were not of this weaving.
Not even bound to their own paths.
They were... controlled by something else.
Something even the Wheel itself could not comprehend.
An Anomaly that had no echoes.
No probabilities.
Just impossibility."
His blind gaze fixed fully on Noah.
But Noah remained calm.
Cold.
Watching.
Variables.
Possibilities.
The Witness had watched across eons— and he looked at Bob or the Peacemaker as possibilities.
He stood, wondering if Infiniverse Megalos or Ruination were the answer.
But then...
Noah's gaze sharpened.
"You thought Bob might be the Variable?
Just because he carried two Dead Absolute Complex True Sources?
You continued to watch all he did because of that?"
Silence fell.
The Witness could feel the disdain bleeding from Noah's words.
He looked down at his hands as he spoke again—softly.
"I have witnessed quintillions of deaths across these breakings.
You and I see the world differently.
We act differently.
I don't expect you to agree with my choices... but they are my weavings, just as your actions are yours.
I may not approve of them... but I would never hold them against you."
Differences.
Viewpoints.
Actions.
Weavings!
Noah's eyes glinted.
"And what actions of mine do you not approve of?"
WAA!
It was a knife-sharp question—and the Witness paused before answering with that same calm, ancient tone.
"It's not a single action.
It's your very existence.
Your state of being.
You are...incomprehensible.
As an Anomaly, you add chaos when we need clarity.
You birth paradoxes.
And binding yourself to the brightest Variables... only deepens the uncertainty.
When the final breaking nears, I believe what is needed is certainty.
Not Anomalies.
But again...
I don't hold it against y—"
"You've talked enough."
HUUM!
A new voice rang out—cutting cleanly through the moment.
It wasn't Noah.
And it wasn't the Witness.
The Infiniverse Megalos Body stepped forward, standing tall beside Noah.
Her eyes shimmered—glorious and unfathomable—brimming with the cold, unrelenting brilliance of Megalos.
And they were locked entirely on the Witness.

chapters.title: Chapter 3688: Infiniverse II
paragraphs: The character of entities that had lived for an unfathomably long time always carried a certain apathy—especially when gazing across the weavings of Existence.

Because when you've witnessed quintillions of deaths, the birth and end of weavings across eons, watching a few trillion—or even more quintillions—fade becomes nothing more than a flicker. A process that once unfolded over millennia now happens in seconds.
And so... they could watch Megalos collapse.
They could witness Frequencies of Existence—intricate expanses laced with Matter, Anti-Matter, and Dark Matter—burst into ruin, their inhabitants screaming silently into oblivion.
And still... feel nothing.
But if Noah stood there, watching as a Frequency began to fall—its Megalos imploding, quintillions about to die—what would he do?
The answer wasn't theoretical. It had already happened. When Bob shattered an entire Frequency by manipulating its Node... what did Noah do?
He restored it.

Even as the Echoes of the Unwritten unfolded, Noah reached through and pulled that Frequency back, reviving the quintillions of beings within it. Every time their battle spilled into another Frequency, he did the same.
Just because he was powerful... just because he'd seen endless death... didn't mean he would stand idle when it stared him in the face.
But not everyone was like him.
The Witness was something else entirely—a being shaped by a Complexity that saw the weavings of Existence through a colder lens.

And now, here he was—speaking of Variables. Of things that could shift the impossible fate of the Wheel. But all he saw in Noah... was an anomaly. A being he couldn't understand. A being tied to the very Variables the Witness prayed would appear.
It was then the Infiniverse Megalos Body stirred. She rose, her expression sharp as steel, her voice slicing through the silence like a drawn blade.
"Just because your weavings can't understand something doesn't make it an anomaly. It simply means... you're lesser."
WAA!
Her voice cracked through the dazzling seas!

"You watched the Wheel break again and again—and did nothing. You had countless years, and still, you never became a Variable, only waited for one. Now, on the eve of the Ninth Breaking, you sulk in solemnity, bemoaning fate. And when one Variable finally arises—one you can't grasp—this is your response? Pathetic."
BOOM!
Her words cut deep.
Her Complexity surged like a storm, rising with her fury.
She turned toward the one she called Master. Her presence quieted... and she dropped to her knees.
"Master, this Variable has been preparing something for you."
Noah moved to raise her gently, smiling.
"You never need to kneel to me. You know that."

"I know," she replied softly. "And I still choose to. What others don't understand... is never an anomaly to me. What they fear, I've always been connected to. And now, I wish to give back—to offer even a fraction of what's been given to me. I want to present you with an Absolute Complex True Source. A Wheel of Existence unlike any other."
HUUM!
As she spoke, her form radiated with a brilliance that pulsed with unspoken power. Noah felt it in his chest and through their grand connection- something calm, something pure!
He nodded.
Then, lifting her hand in his, he looked toward the distant Wheel of Existence and asked.
"What of the Wheel? What of the Witness?"
The one who'd shown them the Breaking. The one who claimed he was waiting for Variables to alter the impossible.
The Infiniverse Megalos Body turned her gaze to him, voice cold as glass.
"He can continue to Witness."
WAA!
"As for the Wheel... I benefited from its First Breaking. And so, I will repay it—by saving it from annihilation."
BOOM!
Words spoken with staggering simplicity... and devastating weight.
She had just declared she would save the Wheel.
And the certainty in her voice made the Witness tremble.
But then her gaze drifted from the Wheel... to Noah.

"It no longer holds meaning for us. I will not touch its Frequencies or its weavings. I will construct my own—on my own foundation—ensuring a purity untainted by any flaw. Complexity will follow. Come, Master. Let me show you."

They were still within the sacred region of the pristine Wheel of Existence. A vast white-gold sea surrounded them—endless and silent. And the Witness, who had been there since the First Breaking, still waited.
Still searching for a Variable.
But the Infiniverse Megalos Body... she turned away from it all. As though it no longer mattered.
Noah nodded.
Then he looked at the distant Wheel, motionless and yet spinning—a contradiction etched in golden fractals.
Bob had come here, searching for something.
Something connected to what he called... The Loom.
Was it hidden within this dying Wheel, now on the brink of its Ninth and Final Breaking?
Noah held that question for only a moment.
Then he took her hand—and together, they vanished.
Leaving the Witness standing alone.
Again.
The white-gold sea stretched in all directions. The shattered fragments of the Wheel drifted endlessly, orbiting a still center. The Witness stood, blind yet somehow dazed.
"They just... left?"
He had waited. Waited to see what would happen if the Infiniverse Megalos Body touched the Wheel.
And yet—she hadn't.
She refused it. Rejected it. Said she'd make her own.
And now...
Even without a Breaking, the Witness was once again... alone.
In the Prime Frequency of the End.
Noah and the Infiniverse Megalos Body returned—hovering before the radiant, multicolored infinity-shaped Infiniverse Vein. The skies rippled with celestial light, Havens floating in the distance.
Her form pulsed—Complexity bleeding from every fiber of her being.

"Since Master is about to comprehend Continuity and Entropy—drawing from the definitions of the Witness and Romulus and forging our own from their definitions...I will begin my advancement with them. Without external interference. Without impurities. I will construct the True Frequency of Continuity and the True Frequency of Entropy—from the foundation of their True Sources."
HUUM!
Her decision ignited something. A storm of purpose built on everything she had become.
And from that moment... the Infiniverse Megalos Body began forging True Frequencies of Existence.
Not borrowed.
Not inherited.
But born from her own making!
Unfathomably grand.
Unfathomably pure.
Unfathomably...magisterial!

chapters.title: Chapter 3689: Infiniverse III
paragraphs: Within the Infiniverse Megalos.
Unique waves of wonder spread outward, the sensations rippling through existence and causing the most perceptive ones to quickly look up, as if sensing the coming changes.

The Queen of Matter, who had been excitedly speaking to a Shadow Guard, froze. Around her, chains connected to golden Books foretelling the grandest Fables came to a halt, even the one in the hands of the Shadow Guard, Night, who was reading them as if judging and evaluating!
The Queen of Matter raised her head in shock. The one she was communicating to did the same.
Inside the intricate vein that held the tremendous weavings of existence, the main bodies of multiple important personages also looked up.
Smiles touched their faces. Some shook their heads, amused.

They stood atop a small haven of obsidian-gold Dreams, shimmering with Dark Matter and Matter. Above them, golden auroras painted the skies. Beneath their feet, brilliant black and gold mountains rolled across the land.
In such a place—
Kazuhiko stopped in front of Henry, pausing their spar. He sheathed his katana, the blade glimmering with the light of Omniverses, and asked lightly.
"Which advancement do we think he's making now? It's happening just as we can't find any more Faceless Lifeforms across frequencies..."
Kazuhiko's words hung in the air. Henry steadied his waves and complexity, shimmering blue and gold, the silent flame of the Singed flickering near him. He shook his head and answered.
"Your guess is as good as mine. But whatever change is coming... feels too significant. Too widespread."
Others heard. Across the haven, beings who were comparing their weavings through sparring looked up, pausing their matches.
Erikson, adorned in blue beach attire, gold flippers clutched in his hands as weapons, spoke out boisterously.
"A transformation of the Infiniverse itself? Maybe he'll take my idea and make a whole frequency of beaches! Endless waves of the sea, white sandy beaches stretching forever!"
A few rolled their eyes.
Nearby, Ayame shimmered gold and added wistfully.
"I wish we could see it happening on the grander scale. I'd love to know—"
Space distorted.
Her words cut off as the figure of the Infiniverse Megalos Body appeared.
Her weavings buzzed with immense complexity and purity. She cast her gaze over those who had gathered here, those using the space to compare their existence through battle.
A blinding illusory screen then erupted above her.

"It will be good for you all," she said, "to observe the emergence of True Frequencies based on the True Sources of Existence. It will make it easier for you to grasp your own True Sources—or to follow the path of the True Severed Origin Osmontian."
It would be a positive thing for them to watch the emergence of True Frequencies of Existence.
Fantastical words. Yet real enough that the screen above them shifted, displaying a scale few could fathom.
A view that stretched across countless light-years. Vast enough to cover multiple Omniverses and still, it was only a zoomed-out image of the massive Infiniverse Vein and the havens surrounding it.
And at that moment—
A violet-purple river of brilliance bloomed from the Infiniverse Vein, stretching outward.
At its base, countless tendrils of complexity and purity intertwined. Growth, happening on a conceptual scale the size of multiple Omniverses.
It contained the budding, terrifying musings of the True Source of Entropy.
The first-ever True Frequency of Existence to be built within the Infiniverse...was Entropy.
Chaos and wonder, woven together.
Maybe it had meaning. Maybe it didn't.
But as many watched, they could not help but ask questions.
Dr. Hall stepped forward, his voice cutting through the awed silence.
"You said True Frequencies of Existence...we've gone into and observed Normal Frequencies and Prime Frequencies. How are they different from True Frequencies?"
A question that caused minds to buzz, thoughts racing.
The Infiniverse Megalos Body, shining with stellar white brilliance, answered calmly:

"Everything is based on Purity and Complexity. In this age of the Wheel of Existence, there are many average Frequencies of Existence and a few Prime Frequencies. But the number of True Frequencies is very low."
She continued.

"Normal Frequencies of Existence are the foundational oceans of weavings that make up the flow of the Wheel. Vast fields containing countless Megalos Domains- Matter, Dark Matter, and Anti-Matter- alongside endless seas of the Expanse, acting as the fulcrum of their complexity and purity. A Normal Frequency holds Average Purity and layered Complexity, but often in a chaotic, unstable, and weak form. Within them, life evolves, decays, and cycles endlessly. Those born within will find it arduous to elevate their existence. The number of Existence Severing, Pioneers, or Source Entities that could emerge... is abysmally low. The Frequency barely expresses what it stands for. Having a True Source emerge from such a place is rare."
She lifted her hand, pointing outward- beyond the haven, toward the grander scale.
The Megalos Ynnere they were within... was contained in the Prime Frequency of the End.

"Prime Frequencies of Existence," she said, "are rarer. They are weavings born from the convergence and refinement of multiple Nodes of Normal Frequencies into singular, higher states. Here, Purity increases sharply as they hold Moderate Purity and Complexity. Contradictions are resolved. Structures of existence grow more resilient and organized. Complexity deepens, forming multi-layered domains that are self-sustaining and potent. The identity of the Frequency becomes actualized. Inhabitants aligned with a Prime Frequency can attain a True Source in time."
Her gaze hardened.

"The Prime Frequency of the End... its inhabitants experience constant apocalypses, dangers, and catastrophes. They must overcome them. And through that struggle, their complexity and purity grow stronger."
They heard such words as they thought back to their own lives and records.
A history of... apocalypses?
Catastrophes?
They thought of everything they had gone through as their expressions could not help but change.
All of that was simply because they were based inside a frequency geared toward expressing itself?
And its expression was what allowed the many life forms within it to increase in power—as through a constant grinding and waves of catastrophe...powerful entities would be born!

chapters.title: Chapter 3690: Infiniverse IV
paragraphs: The gaze of the Infiniverse Megalos Body was calm as she continued.

"The Prime Frequency of Flames bathes everything in a terrifying essence of fire. Only unique lifeforms capable of withstanding the heat of suns are born there. They live their records based on this, and eventually, they too hold the chance of becoming Entities capable of obtaining a True Source. Frequencies of moderate Purity and Complexity—even within them, there are few True Sources capable of being born. But above Prime Frequencies... there are Frequencies born of an established and brilliant True Source of Existence itself."
She paused, her eyes drifting toward the budding True Frequency of Entropy.
All eyes turned upward.
The violet-purple river... had begun to take on the form of a massive pillar.
A pillar- but truly, it was a Spoke, stretching outward from the Infiniverse Vein.
And a Spoke... could only belong to a budding Wheel of Existence.

"True Frequencies of Existence are creations birthed directly from a True Source of Existence," she said, "making them incomparably pure and harmoniously complex. High in Complexity. High in Purity. Unlike Prime or Normal Frequencies, every atom within a True Frequency embodies the fundamental principle of its Source—such as Entropy, Continuity, or Manadynamics. Those born and living within a True Frequency are truly blessed. They gain unique boons, including Existential Transcendence, Existential Immunity, and Limited Absolute Evolution based on the Source's concept. True Frequencies allow for complex beings to rise. From them, powerful True Sources can emerge- giving birth to Nascent Source-Bearer Complexity Entities, Harmonized Sourcebound Icon Entities, even Resplendent Monads and Converged Architects."
She spoke at length. And as she did, the massive pillar...the Spoke—grew larger.
It jutted across light-years of distance, stretching the conceptual size of 1,000 Omniverses... and still expanding.
From it, waves of violet brilliance gushed outward, washing across the surrounding space, even bathing the Infiniverse Vein itself.
Moments later...
BOOM!
An incandescent violet brilliance washed over them all.
The True Source of Entropy.
Had it been a Wild True Source, even the strongest among them would have broken down and collapsed instantly.
But this one had an owner.
It was controlled.
It nurtured rather than destroyed.
They felt it—their weavings of existence reacting, the distant calling of chaos and disorder resonating through their cores.
"True Frequencies," the Infiniverse Megalos Body said, "were abundant before the First Breaking of the Wheel of Existence."
WAA!
Terrifying words.
Words none of them knew—yet!
The First Breaking of the Wheel?
The Wheel broke?
Shock rippled through them. The Infiniverse Megalos Body simply continued.

"There were even Frequency Havens filled with isolated True Sources. Back then, the True Frequencies of Existence exceeded even the high parameters of Purity and Complexity. Their nature approached Limited Absolute levels of Purity and Complexity. From these Frequencies, many Resplendent Monads and Converged Architects were born—beings of tremendously high Purity and Complexity."

"Among them, a single being even exceeded those stages—born from the True Frequency of Lifefyre. But after the First Breaking of the Wheel, progressively lesser True Frequencies bloomed. They lost the luster of Limited Absolute Purity and Complexity. After the Second Breaking, the Third, even the Eighth... very few True Frequencies emerged. Even those that did were mere fractions of what once existed."
She smiled faintly.
"Can you guess... what level of Purity and Complexity we seek for the first True Frequency built under the banner of the True Severed Origin Osmontian?"
Could they guess?
The question hung over them, heavy and profound.
RAA!
An Emperor Penguin thumped its chest with its flippers. A sharp voice rang out
"Limited Absolute! What else could it be under the banner of the True Emperor of Quintessence but this?!"
Its golden eyes radiated pride, fierce and overwhelming.
The Infiniverse Megalos Body turned her gaze to it, and the Penguin's pride wavered slightly under her stare.
Yet she smiled, a rare and brilliant thing to see on her who was serious 99% of the time!
She turned back toward the massive forming Spoke.
Her first Spoke.
The backbone of a new Wheel.
"Yes."
And she gave the affirmation.
"We will forge something unforged since before the First Breaking of the Wheel. A Limited Absolute Purity and Complexity True Frequency of Existence.
It will not only shape itself but spread across the Infiniverse.
It will be the first...of many."
She paused, voice like existential thunder layered beneath weavings of silk.
"In this Infiniverse... there will no longer be Normal or Prime Frequencies.
There will only be True."
HUUM!
Her words resonated profoundly through existence.
They watched as the massive Spoke continued to grow, extending over 5,000 Omniverses in conceptual size.
And inwardly, it was even vaster.
"The True Frequency of Entropy, born from the True Source of Entropy, embodies the elegant dissolution and disorder of existence," she said.
"It is not chaos—it is a return to the Zero-State. The absolute foundation of potential."
The Infiniverse Megalos Body waved her hand, summoning a swirling vortex of violet brilliance, a serpent coiling around her fingers.
HUUM!
The moment the True Source of Entropy appeared in her hands, the world around her shuddered.
Even the obsidian-gold sandy mountains of Dreams were painted violet.
"Beings aligned with this True Frequency can gain the ability to unravel constructs, existence, even memories," she said.
"The unique boon of this True Frequency—the one that will be potent inside of it, but still prevalent across the Infiniverse Megalos as a whole—is Existential Reset."
Her words struck like a hammer.
"The capacity to deconstruct oneself entirely and reforge from pure Zero-State—without losing their existence.
Within this Frequency, destruction and chaos will become sacred rites.
Nothing false will endure the presence of one who undergoes cycles of chaotic unraveling and reformation...until they become Pure and Complex enough to seize the True Source of Entropy itself.
Or even evolve into new meanings of Entropy-Chaos, Disorder, and more."
She smiled, her aura crackling violet with magisterial radiance!
"And mind you...this is just the first True Frequency of the Infiniverse."
Just...the first!
Entropy bloomed as a True Source and as a Spoke of a Wheel.
And yet, as this occurred, silent and unseen waves that represented the birth of an unfathomable Wheel of Existence with its first Spoke spread.
Setting into motion Echoes that even the Infiniverse Megalos could not yet predict the eventual outcomes of!
